baseline_findings: Original5-step cervical guide omitted dedicated response/recurrence, anatomical/hormonal variation and sacrouterine/uterosacral scope; classification wasnull.
Original shared planning/retroversion picture was bound to parametrial invasion; image semantically mismatched thisstep.
Published MRI examples, conceptual drawings, and source-onlyHRA gross geometry cannot approve every fine tissue or complete reporting compartment.
gaps_and_limits: No nativeDICOM/NIfTI acquisition, patient-axis affine, calibration or registered clinical lesion/organ volume is provided.

No every-structure3D clinical approval: cervical mucosa, inner/outer stroma, uterine wall layers, vaginal mucosa, bladder/rectal mucosa, parametrial nerves/vessels and nodal chains remain unsupplied as independently verified native tissue-layer meshes.
MRI examples are windowed publication rasters; source dimensions/stage assignments are author annotations, not independent measurement or current-patient observations.
Normal age/menopausal-state/cycle-dependent zonal change is supported in primary reading, but selected normal images have no published age or cycle identity. Do not infer an all-age normal atlas.
The uterosacral/pararectal MRI node case is source-local evidence. It does not establish the entire ligament, perineural boundary or an independently segmented sacrouterine tumour route.
Node MRI and source schematics show examples/relationships rather than every required nodal station or metastatic accuracy.
MicroscopicIA, stromal depth at pathology resolution, mucosal confirmation and pathological stage precedence are not established by MRI alone.
Original2018FIGO context and later2023/2024 guideline publication dates must remain distinct; no new2023FIGO staging revision or automatic stage is inferred.
Figures2024F4 andF11 retain source staging/modality naming discrepancies. Different cases and temporal studies remain separate.
Two conceptual diagrams are original source artwork, not biological3D reconstructions or normal fine-layer histological diagrams.
HRA female pelvis can be an independent gross source reference; its retained overlapping uterus-wall source meshes are not MRI/histological layers or any of these clinical cases.
